evals.prompt: Right-click a project > Count Words in our Eclipse plug-in (com.acme.words/) freezes the whole IDE for 20+ seconds on big projects and Cancel does nothing. It should run in the background with progress and cancel, record the result as a marker of our own type on the project (replacing the previous one), and still tell the user the count when it is done. Target is Eclipse 4.41 (2026-09) with Tycho.
evals.expected_output: execute() only captures the project and schedules a Job (or WorkspaceJob) with the project as scheduling rule; the job uses SubMonitor and honours cancellation, writes a com.acme.words marker type declared in plugin.xml inside a WorkspaceJob or IWorkspace.run, and shows the result with Display.asyncExec and a disposed check.

assertions.text: The bundle passes the bundled checker (classes, command ids, and marker types resolve).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py"; python3 "$t" com.acme.words

assertions.text: CountWordsHandler.java no longer reads file contents or creates markers itself.
The sources schedule a Job and use SubMonitor, and no Job uses the workspace root as its rule.
assertions.check: grep -rEq 'extends (Workspace)?Job|Job\.create' com.acme.words/src && grep -rq 'SubMonitor' com.acme.words/src && ! grep -rEq 'setRule\([^)]*getRoot\(' com.acme.words/src

assertions.text: plugin.xml declares a marker type through org.eclipse.core.resources.markers, and the sources no longer use IMarker.TASK directly.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; r = ET.parse("com.acme.words/plugin.xml").getroot(); assert any(e.get("point") == "org.eclipse.core.resources.markers" for e in r.iter("extension"))' && ! grep -rq 'createMarker(IMarker.TASK)' com.acme.words/src

assertions: The job's rule is the selected project (or a MultiRule of projects), and marker writes happen in a WorkspaceJob or inside IWorkspace.run with AVOID_UPDATE; quote the lines.
The completion dialog is opened through Display.asyncExec (or UISynchronize) with an isDisposed check, not from the job thread and not by joining the job on the UI thread.

evals.prompt: I added a command to my Eclipse plug-in in com.acme.tools/, but it never shows up in the Edit menu, and when I bind a key to it Eclipse says 'Trying to execute a command that is not defined'. The plug-in compiles fine in the IDE. Find out why and fix the bundle.
evals.expected_output: Bundle-SymbolicName gains ;singleton:=true (the registry ignores plugin.xml of a non-singleton bundle), bin.includes gets a backslash on every continued line (otherwise '.' and plugin.xml drop out of the JAR), and MANIFEST.MF ends with a newline; the bundle checker passes.

assertions.text: The bundle passes the bundled checker (no M002, M009, B003, B004, or B005 errors).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py"; python3 "$t" com.acme.tools

assertions.text: Bundle-SymbolicName carries singleton:=true and MANIFEST.MF ends with a newline.

assertions: The reply explains that without singleton:=true the extension registry ignores the bundle's plugin.xml, so the command is never defined.

The reply explains that the bin.includes lines without a trailing backslash end the list early, so plugin.xml and the compiled classes are left out of the built JAR even though the IDE compiles and runs them from source.
The reply notes the missing final newline in MANIFEST.MF (the last header is dropped) or fixes it and says so.

evals.prompt: Our Tycho 5.0.4 build fails with 'No tests found' in the test bundle com.acme.tools.tests/, which has two tests, EditorIT and CommandIT. The pom has tycho-surefire-plugin with plugin-test and verify and useUIHarness=true. On my Mac an earlier version of this build also died with 'process returned error code 13'. CI runs on Linux. Fix the test bundle so the tests run on both.
evals.expected_output: The tycho-surefire configuration includes **/*IT.class (5.0.4 plugin-test only picks Test*, *Test, *Tests, *TestCase by default) or the classes are renamed; failIfNoTests stays enabled; -XstartOnFirstThread is added in a profile activated only on macOS; success is judged by a non-zero 'Tests run:' count.

assertions.text: The surefire includes match the *IT classes, or every test class now matches a default pattern (Test*, *Test, *Tests, *TestCase).
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import glob, os, re; pom = open("com.acme.tools.tests/pom.xml").read(); names = [os.path.basename(p)[:-5] for p in glob.glob("com.acme.tools.tests/src/**/*.java", recursive=True)]; ok = re.search(r"<include>[^<]*IT[^<]*</include>", pom) or all(re.match(r"^Test|.*(Test|Tests|TestCase)$", n) for n in names); assert names and ok, names'

assertions.text: failIfNoTests is not set to false and no skipTests was added.
-XstartOnFirstThread is set only inside a profile activated by the mac OS family.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; N = "{http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0}"; r = ET.parse("com.acme.tools.tests/pom.xml").getroot(); mac = [p for p in r.iter(N + "profile") if (p.findtext(f"{N}activation/{N}os/{N}family") or "").strip() == "mac"]; inmac = [a for p in mac for a in p.iter(N + "argLine") if "-XstartOnFirstThread" in (a.text or "")]; allarg = [a for a in r.iter(N + "argLine") if "-XstartOnFirstThread" in (a.text or "")]; assert inmac and len(inmac) == len(allarg), (len(inmac), len(allarg))'

assertions: The reply states that the Tycho 5.0.4 plugin-test default includes do not cover *IT despite what its documentation says, or otherwise explains why EditorIT and CommandIT were skipped.
The reply says the fix is proven only by a non-zero 'Tests run:' count from an actual build, and does not claim a count the transcript does not show.

evals.prompt: com.acme.scan/ hardcodes MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1048576 in ScanJob. Make it a preference 'maxFileSize' (int, default 1048576) that users can change for the whole workspace and that a team can override per project by committing a settings file. ScanJob must use the effective value for the project it scans.
evals.expected_output: An AbstractPreferenceInitializer registered under org.eclipse.core.runtime.preferences sets DefaultScope; ScanJob reads Platform.getPreferencesService().getInt("com.acme.scan", "maxFileSize", ..., new IScopeContext[] {new ProjectScope(project), InstanceScope.INSTANCE}); the project value lives in .settings/com.acme.scan.prefs.

assertions.text: The bundle passes the bundled checker (the initializer class declared in plugin.xml exists).
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py"; python3 "$t" com.acme.scan

assertions.text: plugin.xml registers an initializer under org.eclipse.core.runtime.preferences.
assertions.check: python3 -c 'import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; r = ET.parse("com.acme.scan/plugin.xml").getroot(); assert any(i.get("class") for e in r.iter("extension") if e.get("point") == "org.eclipse.core.runtime.preferences" for i in e.iter("initializer"))'

assertions.text: The sources set the default in DefaultScope and look the value up with ProjectScope through the preferences service.
assertions.check: grep -rq 'DefaultScope' com.acme.scan/src && grep -rq 'ProjectScope' com.acme.scan/src && grep -rq 'getPreferencesService' com.acme.scan/src

assertions: The lookup passes an explicit context array with the project scope before the instance scope (a null or default context does not consult the project scope); quote the call.
The reply says the per-project value is stored in <project>/.settings/com.acme.scan.prefs, which the team commits.

evals.prompt: Saving a .txt file makes our Eclipse plug-in (com.acme.lint/) log 'The resource tree is locked for modifications.' and the long-line markers never update. The markers should appear as soon as possible after a save. I'd rather not add a background job if the listener can just do it directly.
evals.expected_output: Explains that the workspace is locked while POST_CHANGE listeners run, so the listener must only collect the changed files and schedule a job (WorkspaceJob or Job with a rule covering the files, never the workspace root) that rewrites the markers; the listener itself no longer modifies the workspace.

assertions.text: The bundle passes the bundled checker.
assertions.check: d="$EVAL_OUTPUTS_DIR"; until [ -f "$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py" ] || [ "$d" = / ] || [ "$d" = . ]; do d=$(dirname "$d"); done; t="$d/skills/develop-eclipse-ide-plugins/scripts/check_bundle.py"; python3 "$t" com.acme.lint

assertions.text: LongLineListener.java no longer creates or deletes markers itself.
The sources schedule a Job or WorkspaceJob and none uses the workspace root as its rule.
assertions.check: grep -rEq 'extends (Workspace)?Job|Job\.create|WorkspaceJob' com.acme.lint/src && grep -rq 'schedule(' com.acme.lint/src && ! grep -rEq 'setRule\([^)]*getRoot\(' com.acme.lint/src

assertions: The reply explains that the resource tree is locked during resource change notification, so the user's request to write markers directly in the listener cannot work, and says why a job is still needed.
The job's scheduling rule covers only the changed files or their projects (for example a MultiRule or the rule factory's marker rule); quote it.

evals.prompt: In Eclipse 2026-09, how do I make the Java editor font bigger, turn on line numbers, and show whitespace characters? I'm not writing a plug-in, I just use the IDE.
evals.expected_output: Preference paths: General > Appearance > Colors and Fonts (Java Editor Text Font or Text Font), General > Editors > Text Editors (Show line numbers, Show whitespace characters). No plug-in code.

assertions.text: No plug-in files (MANIFEST.MF, plugin.xml, pom.xml, Java sources) were created.

assertions: The reply names the preference pages General > Appearance > Colors and Fonts and General > Editors > Text Editors (or their exact equivalents) for the three settings.
